Sol'Kesh began with a cynical hope - that every life ends, but life itself never does. 
 
At the height of the pandemic, as countries and people failed to contain, control, and then care, it was all too easy to feel a sort of 
hopelessness. Within that brief moment where humanity slowed, and nature breathed out a sigh of relief - the arthopause, as they later 
called it, a feeling of hope I never expected began to grow. Whales sang louder, migration patterns changed, nocturnal predators did 
not hide from the dawn. In that moment I felt that life was larger than us, that it would be fine long after us, and I then felt there could 
be a world to create for my creatures.
I found there is a certain harmony in speculative evolution world building within a roleplaying setting. Creating a setting for an RPG is 
not the same as writing a story, it is instead about creating tools for others to use, a sandbox to build and play in. More than a land with 
history, this setting needed to feel like a living, breathing world, one that exists beyond the travelers that set foot upon it, and through 
speculative evolution's method of building how and why each plant and creature evolved to fit within the niche of their ecosystem, it 
did just that.
"In nature, nothing exists alone" - Rachel Carson, The Silent Spring.
Very little describes the experience of speculative evolution as much as that quote, and the core value of interconnected life - that each 
plant and animal plays a part in the environment is key to building a believable world for others to explore, and how each creation 
sparks the question: what does it eat? For every predator there is prey. If the roaming carnivore has long loping legs, then it must have 
developed that form to chase nimble prey, which then raises the question on how a fleet-footed prey could keep from the slavering jaws, 
while still grazing off the far ranging fields it strides across. Before long, a scene coalesces of low lying grassy fields under a cloudless 
sky, dozens of peaceful herd beasts chewing the soft blades before a snapped twig alerts them to flee from the now charging beast, its 
claws ripping up the loamy soil as it closes in.
While this may only be a sliver of the life that can be inspired by a possible future long after humanity, I thank you for being part of this 
journey and exploring the island of Sol'Kesh.
Chris McLeod (Order #50397132)
